collection: NCEE Verbal Aptitude Primary 6 vocabulary practice
note: Original four-option vocabulary practice. Format and topic mapping are provisional. Academic review pending.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: The carpenter found a sturdy stool for the display. Which word is closest in meaning to sturdy?
questions.explanation: Sturdy means firmly built and able to withstand use.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: “Leave a clear path between the desks,” said the teacher. Which word has the same meaning as clear here?
questions.explanation: The path should have nothing blocking it. Clear does not mean transparent in this sentence.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: The committee will postpone the match. Which sentence keeps the same meaning?
questions.answer: The committee will move the match to a later time.
options: The committee will bring the match forward.
The committee will end the match before half-time.
The committee will move the match to a later time.
The committee will move the match to another field.
questions.explanation: To postpone an event is to delay it.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: A notice says, “The hall can accommodate 80 visitors.” Which phrase replaces accommodate without changing the message?
questions.explanation: The notice describes the number of people the hall can hold.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: The guide gave a brief explanation before the tour. Which word is closest to brief?
questions.explanation: Brief refers to a short duration or length.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select a word or phrase that preserves the intended sense in context.
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses “reserve” to mean “book in advance”?
questions.answer: We will reserve seats for the school play.
options: The park is a reserve for wild birds.
The team has a reserve supply of water.
The coach named a reserve player.
We will reserve seats for the school play.
questions.explanation: Only reserving seats means arranging in advance to have a place.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: The paint on the bench is still wet. Which word is the opposite of wet here?
questions.explanation: Dry means free from the moisture that makes the paint wet.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: The pupils found a narrow passage between the shelves. Which word would reverse the description of the passage’s width?
questions.explanation: Wide reverses narrow on the same dimension.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: A sign reads “Entry is permitted after 8 a.m.” Which replacement for permitted reverses the rule?
questions.explanation: Forbidden means entry is not allowed.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: The volunteer said the supply of notebooks was scarce. Which word would express the opposite situation?
questions.explanation: Plentiful means available in large quantities.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: The pupil spoke in a confident voice. Which replacement for confident changes the description to its opposite?
questions.explanation: A hesitant voice suggests uncertainty rather than confidence.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify an opposite meaning for the relevant sense of a word.
questions.prompt: After the clean-up, the number of bottles on the field decreased. Which verb would reverse the direction of change?
questions.explanation: Increased indicates that the count went up rather than down.
